reviews.comment: Mittal was a decent professor. His lectures were solid, but had he gone over more examples in lecture it would have been a lot better since the TA was...yeah. His grading was very fair but the curves were interesting. READ THE TEXTBOOK!!!

reviews.comment: Exam are based off of textbook question, allows a cheatsheet on the exam, pop quiz so attendence vary. expect the curve to not help at all. will add like 5 point or something if class average is like a 52. READ THE TEXTBOOK FOR A DECENT GRADE.

reviews.comment: He didn't help with understanding the material and just made it worse. Exams were very hard and didn't made any sense.

reviews.comment: did not provide practice questions or exams. got mad at my class for averaging 25 on midterm 1  because we "didnt study hard enough" apparently. spent all lecture time deriving formulas and rarely ever did any sort of real questions with us to teach us how to use thise formulas he is deriving.

Dr. Mittal seemed to take on a ruder tone towards the end of the semester, and sometimes his lectures weren't particularly helpful. Reading the textbook was important and reviewing what was discussed in class was necessary to do well on the exams. Tough class but curved well and you will do well if you put in the time to understand the concepts.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Mittal is a caring person but terrible instructor. He likes to do derivation instead of going over problems. I find it way better to just read the textbook, do problems than attending his lectures. It didn't felt like what he was going over helped with the homework or the exams. Moreover, he likes to ramble about random topics.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Mittal was a terrible professor. It was better just to read the textbook then go to lecture. He made the class harder then it needed to be. He only goes over concepts in class and then expects you to do the very hard homework problems. The homework was group work but took about 5-6 hours to complete. Exams were open note but everyone still failed.

Mittal was awesome. Make sure you go to class because he gives attendance quizzes. As long as you read the textbook and work example problems, the tests are pretty straightforward. He is super generous with partial credit on tests, and he even let us retake an exam. Put in work, and you'll get an A. Take him!!!
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Thermodynamics isn't an easy course but professor Mittal is definitely one of the better options for this class. He is very helpful when it comes to feedback/questions and understands the student perspective. Tests were average difficulty, easier if you study the textbook and homework. He offers good partial credit and emphasizes important material
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Mittal was a great professor for CHEN 205. His homework provided excellent practice for exams. His exams were straightforward, and he didn't really try to trick us. His main concern was that we understood the fundamental concepts and explained them thoroughly through showing our work. Dr. Mittal was kind and accessible.
reviews.ratingTags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mittal is a great professor, very caring and grading is very clear. The exams aren't too difficult, often times they are very similar to the HW so make sure to go over those and the extra practice problems he gives out. We had 3 midterms worth 15% each, HW is 15%, Final 35% and random quizzes/attendance 5%. Posts notes on canvas. HARD CLASS!
